title: Reconstitution of Actin-Based Motility with Commercially Available Proteins
protocol: Use ultrapure H2O for all buffers.
Filter all solutions described in steps with a 0.2 µm syringe filter.
Aliquot filtered solutions in portions of 500 µL-2 mL per tube and store at -20 °C.
Weigh 2 g of BSA into a 50 mL conical tube.
Fill the tube to the 20 mL mark with H2O.
Mix until the BSA is dissolved (about 30 min).
Make up the volume to 20 mL.
Prepare Xb buffer as a 10x solution.
Dilute Xb buffer before use by mixing 100 µL of 10x Xb stock solution with 900 µL of H2O.
Mix 100 µL of 10x Xb stock solution, 100 µL of 10% BSA, and 800 µL of H2O to prepare Xb/1% BSA.
Prepare G-buffer with the specified components (2 mM Tris, 0.2 mM CaCl2, 0.2 mM DTT, 2 mM ATP).
Adjust pH of G-buffer to 7.
Prepare motility buffer MB13 with the specified components (10 mM HEPES, 1.5 mM ATP, 3 mM DTT, 1.5 mM MgCl2, 1 mM EGTA, 50 mM KCl, 1% BSA).
Adjust pH of MB13 to 7.5.
Prepare 10x MB13 without BSA for some applications.
Add BSA from a 10% stock solution when reconstituting 1x MB13 from 10x MB13.
Reconstitute actin powder with ultrapure H2O as per manufacturer's instructions.
Pulse centrifuge the tube containing the reconstitution mixture at 4°C.
Let the mixture sit on ice for at least 15 minutes.
Gently mix the solution by pipetting up and down.
Let the mixture sit on ice for another 15 minutes.
Pulse centrifuge the tube again to collect the solution at the bottom of the tube.
Remix the collected solution gently.
Prepare 10-50 μL aliquots of unlabeled actin and store at -80°C.
Prepare 20 μL aliquots of ATTO-labeled actin and store at -80°C.
Dilute an aliquot of resuspended actin ~8-fold in G-buffer spiked with additional ATP and DTT.
Add approximately 10% labeled actin to diluted unlabeled actin on ice.
Let the mixture depolymerize on ice with occasional mixing for a few days to a week.
Measure protein concentration by Bradford assay after depolymerization.
Resuspend Arp2/3 complex (porcine brain) following manufacturer's instructions in 20 μL cold H2O.
Combine solutions from resuspending two tubes of powder to create a larger stock.
Prepare 2 μL aliquots of the combined protein solution and store at -80°C.
Resuspend human recombinant profilin at a 4x higher concentration than specified by the manufacturer's instructions (100 µg protein in 25 µL cold H2O).
Pulse centrifuge and mix on ice as described for actin in step 2.1.
Combine resuspended protein solutions from two tubes of powder before determining protein concentration.
Keep resuspended profilin on ice or refrigerated; do not freeze or allow to warm.
Store properly handled resuspended profilin for at least 6 months to 1 year.
Resuspend human recombinant capping protein following the manufacturer's instructions (50 µg protein in 50 µL cold H2O).
Pulse centrifuge and mix on ice as described for actin in step 2.1.
Chill 50 µL of glycerol on ice and add to resuspended capping protein; mix gently.
Store the combined solution at -20 °C.
Handle stored solution carefully, as it remains stable without freezing and retains activity for months or even years.
Resuspend gelsolin with 20 µg protein in 20 µL cold H2O following manufacturer's instructions.
Pulse centrifuge and mix on ice as described for actin in step 2.1.
Aliquot 5-10 µL of resuspended gelsolin and store at -80 °C.
Resuspend VCA with 500 µg protein in 250 µL cold H2O, doubling the concentration from manufacturer's instructions.
Pulse centrifuge and mix on ice as described for actin in step 2.1.
Make 10 µL aliquots of resuspended VCA and store at -80 °C.
Construct a Bradford standard curve using two overlapping serial dilutions of BSA.
Place four 2 mL tubes for BSA dilution series #1 in row 1 of a microtube rack.
Place four additional 1.5 mL tubes for BSA dilution series #1 next to the 2 mL tubes in row 1.
Place tubes for BSA dilution series #2 as for series #1 in row 3 of the rack.
Place one 2 mL tube for each sample to be measured along with two 1.5 mL tubes in row 5 of the rack.
Add a single 1.5 mL tube in row 5 for the blank.
Measure out Bradford Reagent into the 1.5 mL tubes.
Fill a 15 mL conical tube to the top with Bradford Reagent on ice.
Take up 200 µL Bradford Reagent and eject it back into the conical tube to wet the pipette tip.
Pipette slowly without making bubbles.
Slowly pipette 200 µL of Bradford Reagent into each of the 1.5 mL tubes in the rack.
Return the remaining contents of the 15 mL conical tube to the bottle.
Measure out H2O into the 2 mL tubes.
Add 1,990 µL H2O to the first tube and 900 µL to each of the three other tubes for row 1.
For row 3, add 1,992.5 µL to the first tube and 900 µL to the three other tubes.
Add 2,000 µL H2O to each of the sample tubes in row 5.
Add 10 μL of calibrated 2 mg/mL BSA into the tube containing 1,990 µL H2O to make a 10 µg/mL solution.
Transfer 900 µL of 10 µg/mL BSA solution into the next tube (containing 900 µL H2O) for a 5 µg/mL dilution.
Transfer 900 µL of 5 µg/mL BSA solution into the next tube (containing 900 µL H2O) for a 2.5 µg/mL dilution.
Transfer 900 µL of 2.5 µg/mL BSA solution into the next tube (containing 900 µL H2O) for a 1.25 µg/mL dilution.
Add 7.5 μL of calibrated 2 mg/mL BSA into the tube containing 1,992.5 µL H2O to make a 7.5 µg/mL solution.
Transfer 900 µL of 7.5 µg/mL BSA solution into the next tube (containing 900 µL H2O) for a 3.75 µg/mL dilution.
Transfer 900 µL of 3.75 µg/mL BSA solution into the next tube (containing 900 µL H2O) for a 1.875 µg/mL dilution.
Transfer 900 µL of 1.875 µg/mL BSA solution into the next tube (containing 900 µL H2O) for a 0.9375 µg/mL dilution.
Mix and read absorbance to generate the standard curve.
Add 800 μL H2O to the Bradford reagent tube for the blank.
As efficiently as possible, mix 800 µL of each BSA standard with 200 µL Bradford reagent in the prepared tubes.
Pour each standard into a disposable cuvette and read the absorbance at 600 nm in the spectrophotometer after blanking the machine.
In 2 mL tubes containing 2,000 µL of H2O, gently mix in 2 μl each of Arp2/3 complex and profilin.
Mix in 4 μL of labeled G-actin into the 2 mL tubes.
Add 5 μL each of gelsolin and VCA to the tubes.
Mix in 8 µL of capping protein (human recombinant) to the solution.
Immediately take 800 µL of the prepared solution and mix with Bradford reagent.
Repeat the mixing process for a second reading within 5%-10% of the first reading for each sample.
Pre-chill the centrifuge to 4 °C and set the agitating dry block to 18 °C.
Wash the beads by pipetting 50 μL of Xb buffer into a microcentrifuge tube.
Add 9 μL of 4.5 µm diameter bead suspension or 2 μL of 1 µm diameter bead suspension (2.5 % w/v suspension).
Mix thoroughly and centrifuge the samples at 20,000 x g for 10 min at 4 °C.
Coat the beads by removing the supernatant without disturbing the bead pellet.
Resuspend the bead pellet in 40 µL of 2 µM SpVCA (or 7 µM VCA) in Xb buffer by gentle pipetting.
Agitate at 18 °C, 1,000 rpm for 20 min.
Centrifuge the mixture at 20,000 x g for 10 min at 4 °C and remove the supernatant carefully.
Resuspend the beads in 50 µL of cold Xb/1% BSA.
Centrifuge again at 20,000 x g for 10 min at 4 °C and remove the supernatant.
Repeat the washing step once more.
Resuspend the coated bead pellet in 120 µL cold Xb/1% BSA to maintain consistent surface area per microliter of solution.
Store the resuspended beads on ice or in a refrigerator.
Prepare the motility mix by combining components to achieve a total volume of 8.4 µL for observation clarity.
Mix approximately 5 µM G-actin (10% labeled fluorescent actin) with 5 µM profilin, 50 nM Arp2/3 complex, and 25 nM capping protein (or 240 nM gelsolin).
Mix 3.2 µL of MB13 on ice.
Add 1.5 µL of profilin at 30 µM diluted in MB13 to the mixture.
Pipette 1 µL of capping protein at 0.21 µM diluted in MB13 or gelsolin diluted to 2 µM in MB13 into the mixture.
Add 1 µL of Arp2/3 complex at 0.47 µM diluted in MB13 to the mixture.
Vortex just before use and pipette 0.2 µL of bead suspension into the mixture.
Mix 1.5 µL of actin at 30 µM in G-buffer with the previous components.
Mix well but quickly once all components are added.
Spot the entire motility reaction mixture on a slide.
Cover the spotted area with an 18 mm x 18 mm coverslip.
Seal the coverslip with melted VALAP using a small paintbrush.
Observe motility reactions immediately using a 100x objective on either an upright or an inverted microscope equipped with phase contrast and/or epifluorescence microscopy.
Collect time-lapse movies in phase contrast microscopy to evaluate individual bead speeds.
Take frames every 1-10 seconds based on bead speed and resolution requirements.
Use the tracking tool in an image processing program to obtain bead speeds and trajectories.
